facts.text: Christine Chenitz has a master’s degree in Social Work.
Christine Chenitz currently has a psychotherapy practice.
Christine Chenitz works with people who have experienced trauma including religious and spiritual trauma and adverse religious experiences.
Christine Chenitz was raised in a strict form of conservative Christianity within an insular community structure.
Christine Chenitz has lived experience with religious trauma.
Christine Chenitz deconverted from Christianity in her 20s.
Christine Chenitz joined Marlene’s Helping Professionals Group.
Christine Chenitz joined Journey Free to further support people recovering from adverse religious experiences.
Christine Chenitz moderates the Making Connections/Friends group.
Christine Chenitz moderates the Dealing with Believers And The Church group.
Janice Selbie was born and raised in a Canadian evangelical Christian home.
Janice Selbie’s parents believed the Bible was literal and inerrant.
Janice Selbie married a man who became a pastor.
Janice Selbie and her husband were married for nearly 20 years.
Janice Selbie raised two daughters.
Janice Selbie experienced a series of tragedies in her late 30s.
Janice Selbie’s doubt in the God of the Bible shook her loose from her cognitive dissonance.
Janice Selbie started researching other religions after her divorce.
Janice Selbie explored what she had denied herself.
Janice Selbie went back to school to become a Registered Professional Counsellor.
Janice Selbie discovered Marlene online.
Janice Selbie attended some of Marlene’s retreats in San Francisco.
Janice Selbie developed the Divorcing Religion Workshop.
Coco Owen grew up in the Seventh-day Adventist Church.
Coco Owen left the Seventh-day Adventist Church after a crisis of faith at age 21.
Coco Owen pursued graduate degrees in comparative literature and clinical psychology.
Coco Owen is a licensed psychologist in Los Angeles, CA.
Coco Owen has an all-telehealth private practice.
Coco Owen has two young-adult children.
Coco Owen loves animals.
Coco Owen joined the Journey Free community.
Coco Owen moderates the Creativity group.
Kevin Davison recalls an early Southern Illinois Pentecostal church where he first spoke in tongues at age 7.
Kevin Davison first spoke in tongues after a laying on of hands in the children’s church basement.
Kevin Davison graduated from CFNI in 1995.
Kevin Davison became a failed missionary evangelist to Brazil by choice.
Kevin Davison chose a different career in technology.
Kevin Davison attended retreats with accompanying therapy/coaching from Marlene.
Kevin Davison is recovering with a community of Reclaimers.
Kevin Davison facilitates conference calls.
Kevin Davison moderates groups.
Kevin Davison provides technical web support.
Chase Marks was raised as a Jehovah’s Witness.
Chase Marks decided to leave the religion in his mid-20s.
Chase Marks faced losing his family, friends, community, world view, and sense of self after leaving Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Chase Marks began a healing journey after finding that there must be more to life.
Chase Marks began looking into religions and spiritual practices outside of Christianity.
Chase Marks worked with and studied under traditional healers and medicine people.
Chase Marks realized his healing would come from his own experiences and his own beliefs.
Chase Marks offers services as a religious recovery consultant.
Chase Marks is a trained health and wellness coach.
Chase Marks facilitates the Saturday support group for Release & Reclaim.
Chase Marks moderates the Sex and Pleasure group for Release & Reclaim.
Chase Marks moderates the Death, Mortality, Fear of Hell group for Release & Reclaim.
Jessica was raised as an evangelical Christian.
Jessica identified as a progressive Christian for most of her adult life.
Jessica left religion altogether in 2017.
Jessica is a Clinical Social Worker practicing in Southeastern Pennsylvania.
Jessica’s practice focuses mostly on trauma with children and teens.
Jessica read Marlene’s book Leaving the Fold in the summer of 2021.
Jessica joined the Journey Free group to both give and receive support from people with similar lived experiences.
Jessica lives with her three kids and her husband in Southeastern, PA.
Tim grew up in an evangelical Christian home.
Tim attended various conservative churches in his younger years including Charismatic, Presbyterian, and Methodist.
Tim moderates the Spirituality board on this site.
Tim helps out with moderating other boards too.
Tim is a retired software engineer.
Tim ran a travel agency with his wife for over 20 years.
Tim traveled to many countries.
Tim met people of different cultures.
Tim follows a non-dogmatic approach to exploring spirituality.
MK (Mary Karol) McGee was raised as a conservative Evangelical Christian.
MK (Mary Karol) McGee adhered to conservative Evangelical Christianity until she started deconstructing in the early 2000s.
MK (Mary Karol) McGee joined Release and Reclaim in December 2019.
MK (Mary Karol) McGee participated in a book study of Marlene’s book.
MK (Mary Karol) McGee enjoys compassion, connection, and learning how to be human day by day.
The group is a virtual group.
The group is devoted to healing and growth.
As a group member, a person has access to profiles of other members and their stories of recovery from religion.
As a group member, a person has access to online discussions pertaining to topic areas and can join a topic or start a new topic at any time.
As a group member, a person has access to exercises for healing and growth related to the topics being discussed.
As a group member, a person has access to articles of interest and humor.
As a group member, a person has access to creative pages to view members’ work and post creative writing and art.
As a group member, a person has access to resources such as book reviews, podcasts, videos, and conferences.
As a group member, a person has access to conference calls.
The group discusses whatever is on a person’s mind during conference calls and provides support for each person.
